result:
The proposed answer is not correct. The expression for \(P(A)-Q(A)\) in the solution is wrong, so the final value is wrong too.

**Derivation.** Sort the elements as \(a_1<\dots<a_n\) with \(n=2025\). The coefficient of \(a_i\) in \(P-Q\) is computed as follows, taking the median of an even subset to be the average of its two middle elements.

- Odd subsets with \(a_i\) as median contribute \(\sum_k \binom{i-1}{k}\binom{n-i}{k}=\binom{n-1}{i-1}\).
- Even subsets contribute \(\tfrac12\binom{n-1}{i}\) when \(a_i\) is the lower middle element and \(\tfrac12\binom{n-1}{i-2}\) when it is the upper middle element.

So \(c_i=\binom{n-1}{i-1}-\tfrac12\left[\binom{n-1}{i}+\binom{n-1}{i-2}\right]\).

With \(\max(A)=1\), the maximum is attained in the limit by a step sequence: \(a_i=0\) for \(i<j\) and \(a_i=1\) for \(i\ge j\). Its value is the tail sum of the \(c_i\). Telescoping gives
\[
\sum_{i\ge j}c_i=\tfrac12\left[\binom{n-1}{j-1}-\binom{n-1}{j-2}\right].
\]
There is no extra \(+\tfrac12\) term, unlike in the proposed formula.

**Checking the proposed values.** Take \(m=j-1\) and \(n-1=2024\). Then \(\binom{2024}{m}-\binom{2024}{m-1}=\binom{2024}{m}\cdot\frac{2025-2m}{2025-m}\).

- At \(m=1011\) the factor is \(3/1014\), not \(3/1013\), so the proposed simplification is already wrong.
- The proposed choice \(m=1011\) is also not the maximizer. At \(m=1010\) the difference is \(\binom{2024}{1011}\cdot\frac{1011}{1014}\cdot\frac{5}{1015}\approx 0.00491\binom{2024}{1011}\). At \(m=1011\) it is \(\binom{2024}{1011}/338\approx 0.00296\binom{2024}{1011}\). So the claimed maximizer is not optimal.

The proposed answer therefore has a wrong formula, a wrong ratio, and a wrong maximizer.

VERDICT: REJECT
